title: You got to fight
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: This is a story, not a lesson. Read it and think about something you would not let go of.

groups.heading: I'm gonna tell a little anecdote

lines.text: I said I did not ask permission, but I would tell a little anecdote. When we started the company, we realized something unfortunate was going on. My ex-partners were trying to steal, and they stole, a very big client base of jobs that belonged to the company.
There were two ways to go about it, I said. The company was counting an enormous amount of money. I won't get into the details.
I told my partner, as a friend and a mentor: you have to fight. You cannot sit with your arms crossed and say, oh, I got screwed. It's a principles thing.
So we sued them, I said, and so far we have won the lawsuit. Eventually there is a very big check coming.
But you don't give up, I said. That is what we are learning from the author right now.
What would you fight for on principle?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write something that was taken from you or your business.
Write why you did or did not fight for it.
Write what principle is at stake.

check.q: What did I tell my partner to do?
What did I say it was?
What did I say about giving up?

recap: Fight on principle. You don't give up.
